jobs.title: Data Integration/Engineering Intern at New York City Fire Pension Fund
jobs.description: Employer: New York City Fire Pension Fund Expires: 08/28/2026 The NYC Fire Pension Fund is looking for a Data Integration / Engineering Intern.About the RoleWe are looking for a practical, detail-oriented Data Integration / Engineering Intern to join our team. In this role, you won't need years of industry experience, but you will need strong logical reasoning, a solid grasp of SQL, and a knack for troubleshooting data issues.You will work directly with our data pipelines to help clean, process, and ensure the reliability of our datasets. If you love solving puzzles using the process of elimination and enjoy turning messy data into structured, reliable information, this is a great fit for you. Key ResponsibilitiesData Processing & ETL: Assist in building, maintaining, and monitoring data pipelines to ingest and transform data from multiple sources.Data Quality & Flagging: Identify anomalies, duplicate entries, or missing data. Write logic to flag questionable records for further review without breaking downstream processes.Troubleshooting: Use systematic problem-solving and process of elimination to root-cause why a pipeline failed or why a dataset looks incorrect.Database Maintenance: Write and optimize basic to intermediate SQL queries to analyze, clean, and validate stored data.Documentation: Keep brief, clear notes on data quality rules, flagged record criteria, and pipeline workflows.Communicating: You’ll be engaging office staff in learning about their work habits, how to handle a conversation and working in-person. The primary form of engagement is in-office with emphasis in face-to-face dialogue. You will be presenting work as well to your team members, staff, supervisors and leadership. What We’re Looking ForTechnical SkillsSQL Foundations: Working knowledge of SQL (SELECT, JOINs, GROUP BY, WHERE filtering, CASE statements, and basic aggregations).Data Handling: Basic understanding of data structures (e.g., CSV, JSON, relational tables).Scripting (Bonus): Familiarity with Python, Bash, or another scripting language is a plus, but not required.Mindset & Problem-SolvingProcess of Elimination: Excellent logical reasoning skills—you know how to isolate variables step-by-step to figure out where data is breaking.Attention to Detail: High instinct for spot-checking numbers and catching inconsistencies before they reach production.Common Sense & Ownership: You know when to ask for help, when to double-check your work, and how to apply practical logic to business rules.Curiosity: A natural desire to understand why data looks the way it does.Multiple Priorities: You’ll be exposed to a startup like environment where we all handle multiple projects at the same time given the amount of slack that may manifest itself by resources you might not have control.What You’ll GainHands-on experience with real-world, enterprise-level data integration pipelines and development methodologies.Mentorship from experienced data engineers and analysts.Exposure to modern data stack tools and cloud environments.Practical experience handling large-scale data quality.Confidence in public speaking and presenting.

jobs.title: USDA-ARS Agricultural Data Solutions Internship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 08/29/2026 Application Deadline 9/25/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription *Applications are reviewed on a rolling-basis.ARS Office/Lab and Location: An opportunity is currently available with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Research Service (ARS) Partnerships for Data Innovations (PDI), an enterprise-level data solutions provider in the National Measurement and Monitoring Innovations Project within the Agroecosystem Management Research Unit (AMRU) in Lincoln, Nebraska. This opportunity may also be remote.The Agricultural Research Service (ARS) is the U.S. Department of Agriculture's chief scientific in-house research agency with a mission to find solutions to agricultural problems that affect Americans every day from field to table. ARS will deliver cutting-edge, scientific tools and innovative solutions for American farmers, producers, industry, and communities to support the nourishment and well-being of all people; sustain our nation’s agroecosystems and natural resources; and ensure the economic competitiveness and excellence of our agriculture. The vision of the agency is to provide global leadership in agricultural discoveries through scientific excellence.PDI supports ARS researchers and stakeholders by providing technical assistance to develop, host, and maintain public-facing custom data solutions such as web-based applications, digital research tools, and software that support the ARS core mission. Services by PDI provide support to our scientists who are highly experienced in their research fields but may not have the technical, information technology (IT), or data science experience to build digital tools that optimize research efficiency and maximize the impact of their ARS research.Research Project: You will collaborate with the Partnerships for Data Innovations (PDI) team to train in the agile and innovative development of customized data solutions that promote collaboration and stewardship of ARS's research data and other knowledge assets. PDI is the only in-house public-facing enterprise-level data solutions provider for ARS scientists. Learning Objectives: You will learn a diversity of technical skillsets to develop, host, and maintain both internal and public-facing custom data solutions such as web-based applications, digital research tools, and software that support the ARS core mission. Specific training may include, but is not limited to, database development, web application development, and software development. You may request a remote training appointment.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Kyle Stoltz (kyle.stoltz@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: September 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for one year, but may be renewed upon recommendation of ARS and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Participant Stipend: You will receive a monthly stipend commensurate with educational level and experience. The anticipated stipend range is $6,617 - $6,680 monthly.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and ARS. Participants do not become employees of USDA, ARS, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process, please email ORISE.ARS.Plains@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.Qualifications The qualified candidate should be currently pursuing or have received an associate's or bachelor's degree in the one of the relevant fields. Preferred skills:Preferred educational background in computer sciences or related field.Any educational or work experience with agricultural data is a plus.Knowledge in computer programming (Python, HTML, Java, Powershell) and IT science/security experience also a plus.Stipend $6,617.00 – $6,680.00 MonthlyPoint of Contact JaneenEligibility Requirements Citizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Associate's Degree or Bachelor's Degree.

jobs.description: Employer: Barksdale CRANE Expires: 08/29/2026 Job Title: Electrical Engineering Intern Location: Los Angeles, CA FLSA Status: Exempt Reports To: VP Engineering _______________________________________________________________________ INTRODUCTION An exciting opportunity exists for an Electrical Engineering Intern to join a global engineering team. This role provides hands-on experience in electronics design, PCB layout, and embedded hardware development for advanced sensing, actuation, control, and monitoring products. The position offers exposure to hardware design, embedded systems, and compliance testing in industrial environments, ideal for students eager to apply classroom knowledge to real-world projects. PRINCIPLE RESPONSIBILITIES: • Assist with schematic capture and PCB layout using tools such as Altium or Eagle. • Support development and testing of embedded firmware for microcontrollers in C/C++. • Help prototype and validate hardware designs, ensuring proper integration with mechanical components. • Participate in functional and environmental testing (EMC, vibration, shock, climatic). • Provide support for sustaining engineering tasks, including troubleshooting and documentation. • Perform design research for ongoing projects and assist engineers in identifying technical solutions. • Collaborate on complex modification projects to meet custom application needs of key customers. • Learn and execute test protocols in the engineering lab; generate test reports per Engineering SOP. • Complete at least one technical and one business-related independent project; present progress to the executive team. • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives focused on streamlining engineering products or processes. CRITICAL FACTORS FOR SUCCESS • Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical or Electronic Engineering (or related field). • Must possess a GPA of 3.5 or higher. • Familiarity with basic analog/digital circuit concepts. • Exposure to PCB design tools and microcontroller programming through coursework or projects. • Comfortable using common lab equipment (oscilloscopes, power supplies, logic analyzers, debuggers). • Knowledge of embedded C programming IDEs (microcontroller experience is a plus). • Understanding of ultra-low power mixed-signal electronics and industrial automation concepts preferred. • Familiarity with embedded designs (microprocessor, RAM, EEPROM), analog circuit design (Op Amps, Filters, SPICE simulation), and digital circuit design fundamentals. • Strong problem-solving skills and eagerness to learn. PAY RANGE: $22.00 – $26.00 per hour (based on experience and qualifications) WHAT YOU’LL GAIN • Real-world experience in electronics design and embedded systems. • Mentorship from senior engineers. • Opportunity to contribute to global projects and learn industry standards. • Exposure to compliance testing and product development processes. About Barksdale Founded in 1949, Barksdale is a leading manufacturer of precision control products for industrial applications. As part of Crane Co.’s Process Flow Technologies segment, Barksdale specializes in solutions for pressure, temperature, level, and flow control. Our product portfolio includes switches, transducers, valves, regulators, and air suspension systems, serving demanding applications in oil & gas, transportation, and general industrial markets. With headquarters in Los Angeles, California, and operations in Germany, China, and India, Barksdale combines global reach with local expertise. The Company operates through two strategic growth platforms: Aerospace & Electronics and Process Flow Technologies. Crane has approximately 7,000 employees across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia. For more information, visit www.craneco.com. jobs.title: Software Engineering Intern - Summer 2027 at Medtronic
jobs.description: Employer: Medtronic Expires: 09/03/2026 We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 16 Oct 2026 Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact. A Day in the LifeOur summer internships are full-time (40 hours/week), paid positions lasting 10-11 weeks. We offer competitive compensation, educational and social programming throughout the summer, as well as housing assistance and relocation support for eligible interns. Software Engineering interns contribute to experienced teams across software development, AI/data science, cloud, quality, DevOps, systems, testing, and firmware engineering. Examples of work in each area are listed below. Software Engineer Designs, develops, tests, debugs, and implements operating system components, software tools, and utilities. Determines systems software design requirements. Software Cloud Engineer Supports development and execution of the organization’s cloud strategy from a technical perspective, including design, planning, integration, maintenance, and support of cloud architecture. Works with stakeholders to evaluate cloud systems and identify appropriate solutions. Software Quality Engineer Develops, modifies, applies, and maintains standards for software systems quality operating methods, processes, and procedures. Evaluates software systems activities including requirements, design, development, documentation, integration, test, verification, and validation. Software Development Operations Engineer Introduces and maintains processes, tools, and methodologies that support the software development life cycle. Conducts requirements gathering and analysis to understand the software domain, hardware and software interfaces, and overall software characteristics. Software Systems Engineer Develops software and tools in support of design, infrastructure, and technology platforms, including operating systems, cloud-based tools, and Internet-related tools. Designs, develops, troubleshoots, and debugs software programs for enhancements and new products. Software Test Engineer Tests the functionality and performance of software applications or systems software. Develops and executes test plans and scripts designed to detect problems in software applications and systems software. AI/Data Science Engineer Develops and programs integrated software algorithms to structure, analyze, and leverage data in product and system applications. Develops and communicates descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive insights or algorithms. Location and Work Model Most internship positions are based at primary hubs in Minnesota, California, Colorado, Connecticut, and Massachusetts; with additional opportunities available in Arizona, Florida, Michigan, Tennessee, and Texas. Candidate location preferences are strongly considered during the interview and offer process; however, flexibility increases the number of potential opportunities available. All interns must reside in the U.S. for the duration of the internship. Medtronic is working a minimum of 4 days a week onsite as part of its commitment to professional growth, cross-functional collaboration, and engineering the extraordinary. Must Have: Minimum Requirements To be considered for a Summer 2027 engineering internship, your resume must clearly demonstrate how you meet each of these basic requirements. Working toward a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a related engineering major with an anticipated graduation date of Winter 2027, Spring 2028, Winter 2028, or Spring 2029. Ability to participate full time, 40 hours per week, as part of the intern cohort from June 1-August 13 for semester system programs or June 14-August 20 for quarter system programs. Applicants for Medtronic’s Summer Internship Program must be currently authorized to work in the United States. Medtronic does not sponsor work authorization for internship positions. Individuals on temporary visa classifications, including E, F‑1 (CPT or OPT), H‑1, H‑2, L, B, J, or TN, as well as anyone who requires employment sponsorship now or in the future, are not eligible for the Program. Nice to Have: Preferred Requirements Minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA. Flexibility in geographic location. Experience with one or more programming languages or technical tools, such as C, C++, C#/.NET, SQL, JavaScript, Java, Python, Swift, HTML/CSS, Microsoft Visual Studio, Jenkins, GitLab, or similar tools. Academic project, internship, research, lab, or work experience related to software development, testing, automation, DevOps, cloud, firmware, systems engineering, AI, data science, or software quality. Experience using version control, debugging tools, test documentation, requirements gathering, or software development lifecycle processes. Experience creating technical documentation, project summaries, test reports, code documentation, or engineering presentations. For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required. Physical Job RequirementsThe above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position, but they are not an exhaustive list of all the required responsibilities and skills of this position. The physical demands described within the Responsibilities section of this job description are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. For Office Roles: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer, and communicate with peers and co-workers. Contact your manager or local HR to understand the Work Conditions and Physical requirements that may be specific to each role. U.S. Work Authorization & SponsorshipAt Medtronic, we are committed to fostering an environment where employees can thrive and make a meaningful impact. In alignment with our enterprise-wide workforce planning approach, U.S. work authorization sponsorship (H-1B, TN, J, etc.) is offered exclusively for Principal-level roles and above, where specialized expertise aligns with long-term business needs. Roles below the Principal level require candidates to possess unrestricted U.S. work authorization at the time of hire and for the duration of employment.‌Recruitment Fraud AlertWe are aware of phishing scams targeting job seekers. Please keep the following in mind: Apply only through official Medtronic channels. All legitimate Medtronic recruiting communications come from approved Medtronic platforms and official @medtronic.com email addresses. Medtronic will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information (such as bank account or Social Security details) during early stages of the hiring process. Any such requests are not legitimate. If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Medtronic, do not respond, click links, or open attachments. If you have any questions, concerns regarding the authenticity of a communication alleged to have been made by or on behalf of Medtronic, please contact us immediately at AskHR@medtronic.com. ‌Benefits & Compensation Medtronic offers a competitive Salary and flexible Benefits PackageA commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values. We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help to create. We offer a wide range of benefits, resources, and competitive compensation plans designed to support you at every career and life stage. Salary ranges for U.S (excl. PR) locations (USD):$26.50-$45.25 The base salary range is used nationally in the United States, excluding Puerto Rico. The Medtronic Internship Program offers an hourly rate of pay that falls within the range of $26.50 to $45.25 per hour. The hourly rate offered will be determined by the position and is subject to variation based on the number of years of school completed. The following benefits and additional compensation are available to those regular employees who work 20+ hours per week: Health, Dental and vision insurance, Health Savings Account, Healthcare Flexible Spending Account, Life insurance, Long-term disability leave, Dependent daycare spending account, Tuition assistance/reimbursement, and Simple Steps (global well-being program). Regular employees are those who are not temporary, such as interns. Temporary employees are eligible for paid sick time, as required under applicable state law, and the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Please note some of the above benefits may not apply to workers in Puerto Rico. This role reports to Hyfé’s Senior Scientist and Lab Manager working closely with the R&D Team.ResponsibilitiesCollaborate with technical team to plan, prepare, and perform experiments.Assist with pilot operations.Follow all safety practices, including wearing proper PPE, completing safety trainings, and contributing to the ongoing development of safety systems and protocols.Manage routine lab maintenance and upkeep, including inventory, cleaning, and organization.Complete tasks within agreed timelines, tracking and communicating progress.Maintain inventory of chemicals and supplies, and work with vendors as neededRecord, compile and analyze experimental data and present findings to the R&D team.Assist with other areas of lab management as needed.Perform duties in keeping with Hyfé’s values, policies and EHS protocols.RequirementsCurrently working on collegiate level chemical engineering or chemistry courses with laboratory component.Capable of safely lifting and carrying laboratory materials and equipment weighing up to 40 lbs.Ability to maintain a regular full-time schedule of 40 hours per week during standard business hours.Innovative mindset with a can-do attitude and passion for Hyfé’s vision.Strong interpersonal, communication, and time management skills.Authorization to work in the US (unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position).About HyféSee our coverage from the World Economic Forum here.Every year, approximately one billion tons of nutrient-rich fruit and vegetable waste is discarded or under-utilized across global food systems. For processors, getting rid of this waste is costly and emissions-intensive, creating significant environmental impact with little to no economic return. Yet these waste streams contain valuable compounds that could transform the economics of businesses across the food system and help catalyze the production of sustainable chemicals and materials. Hyfé exists to change that.Hyfé transforms food waste into high-value ingredients using a label-friendly, thermochemical refining process. Our products range from bioactives to fibers, and are being commercialized to make the food we eat healthier for people and the planet. Our team of scientists and engineers brings decades of expertise from the oil refining and chemical industries, specializing in scaling industrial processes and pioneering sustainable solutions.At Hyfé, you’ll have the opportunity to build at the earliest stages of a mission-driven company—working alongside a world-class team, shaping real products, and helping define how the next generation of ingredients are made.Our mission is simple: To transform carbon we waste into carbon we need. __________________________________________________________________Hyfé is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: Scheduling Engineer Intern at Ryan Companies
jobs.description: Employer: Ryan Companies Expires: 09/06/2026 Job DescriptionAs a Construction Scheduling Intern at Ryan, you'll work side by side with our scheduling team and gain hands-on experience across the full lifecycle of real, active construction projects. You'll learn how a project comes together from the macro level — overall milestones, sequencing, and strategy — down to the micro level of the daily field activities that drive the schedule. Along the way you'll build real skills in CPM scheduling, scheduling software, contracts and the standards our teams use every day. Interns who excel in this role are strong candidates for a full-time position. Some things you can expect to do:Work alongside an experienced scheduler to learn and apply Ryan's scheduling standards, tools, and process (Fundamentals, the Ryan Process, and P6).Spend time on active jobsites, connecting the schedule to what's actually being built in the field.Support project teams in creating, updating, and reviewing schedules, including during the proposal and preconstruction stages.Help keep project schedules accurate and current by assisting with regular progress updates.Assist in preparing monthly project schedule health reports and learn how scheduling data is used to monitor project performance.Sit in on collaborative planning sessions with project teams, subcontractors, and owners to see how sequencing, manpower, and durations are developed against project milestones.Observe "peer review" sessions on complex and high-profile projects to understand how schedules are stress-tested.Help capture and organize completed project schedule data to support the Data Analytics team's continuous-improvement efforts.Build a foundation in construction scheduling and stay curious about how the industry and its tools continue to evolve. What you'll gain:A complete, ground-level view of how a construction project is planned, sequenced, and delivered.Direct mentorship from Ryan's scheduling team and exposure to leaders across operations and the field.Practical experience with the software and methods used on real projects, not just in a classroom. What we're looking for:Currently pursuing a degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Architectural Engineering, or a related field.Genuine interest in construction scheduling, planning, and project controls.Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.Comfortable splitting time between an office setting and active construction sites.Eager to learn, ask questions, and take initiative. Compensation:The hourly wage is $20-$25/hour . The hourly rate may vary within the anticipated range based on factors such as the ultimate location of the position and the selected candidate’s knowledge, skills, and abilities.

jobs.title: Construction Co-Op Warren NJ - Summer 2027 at Higley Construction
jobs.description: Employer: Higley Construction Expires: 09/06/2026 About the Company – Celebrating 100 Years of Building Community & 100% Employee-Owned Higley Construction has been one of the most experienced and respected construction firms in the region. The company surpassed 100 years in business—a century shaped by an unwavering commitment to its core values of people, ethics, respect, commitment, and excellence. Since its founding in 1925, Higley Construction has partnered with clients to bring their goals and visions to life, consistently guided by honesty, integrity, and mutual respect. At Higley Construction, we build more than buildings — we build trust, relationships, and communities. From the offices where you work, to the schools where you learn, and the hospitals where you heal, we create environments where people can live, work, and thrive. With every project, we go beyond bricks and mortar to connect people and place, delivering spaces that stand the test of time. Position Overview:The Operations Co-Op is designed to introduce college students to office and field experiences in the commercial construction profession. The Co-Op rotation exposes the student to a wide array of professional interactions among management, project managers, field workers, consulting professionals, clients, and related trades, exploring the role of each within a project. The Co-Op will work under corporate managers, project managers, or field superintendents on a variety of construction tasks. Ultimately, this program intends to enhance the Co-Op’s individual abilities by gaining on-site knowledge of how a project idea becomes a construction reality.The Co-Op will either be assigned to an active construction project site and/or a construction specialized department located in Warren, New Jersey for the Summer of 2027!Responsibilities:Learn and understand project design drawings and specifications to accurately interpret and gather necessary information. Capture and document project site photographs to record construction progress and existing conditions before starting work in new areas.Acquire knowledge of the submittal process for obtaining approval of building materials.Prepare and effectively maintain a submittal log.Assist the Superintendent and Project Manager in preparing and processing along with maintaining Request for Information (RFI) logs for tracking purposes.Collaborate with the Project Manager and Superintendent to prepare weekly meeting minutes for subcontractor and Owner-Architect-Contractor (OAC) meetings.Prepare daily reports summarizing project activities.Attend safety meetings, walkthroughs, and weekly toolbox talks.Review weekly safety audits with the Superintendent to ensure compliance and address any issues.Participate in quality meetings and quality walkthroughs to ensure project standards are met.Adhere strictly to safety procedures, includes personal protection apparel and equipment.Software’s Utilized: Bluebeam, Microsoft Office, Flashtract, Plangrid, Microsoft SharePoint, Jonas Premier, HammerTech (Safety/Quality), Oracle P6 (Project Controls), Onscreen-Takeoff (Preconstruction).Performs other related duties as assigned.Skills and Abilities:Strong competency in business writing and public presentation skills, with a drive to become a compelling presenter, motivator, and team leader. Demonstrates exceptional personal work habits and a forward-thinking approach.Proficient in, or eager to learn, various construction software applications.Exhibits proactive, curious, and innovative thinking, with a strong desire to learn and contribute.Ability to work independently, with direction and supervision, and in a team environment.Excellent mathematical, problem-solving, and relationship management skills.Skilled in assessing and solving problems with a strategic mindset.Qualifications: Enrolled and actively pursuing a college or university accredited degree program in civil engineering, construction management, or a related architectural/engineering field.Desire to work in construction management and to learn about the construction industry.

jobs.title: Horticulture Intern at The Columbus Museum
jobs.description: Employer: The Columbus Museum Expires: 09/06/2026 Purpose StatementThe Columbus Museum is a mature, successful art and history museum with an Olmsted historic garden in a growing community in West Central Georgia with many cultural amenities.The ideal candidate will work as a team member, performing a variety of skilled and semi-skilled landscape tasks to implement the maintenance and planting of natural areas, grounds and garden beds according to plans. This position is non-exempt and will include both weekday and weekend hours. Hours TBD upon hiring. Must work outdoors in all weather conditions and routinely lift up to 40 pounds. Essential Functions ● Adheres and promotes the mission, vision and values of The Columbus Museum, Inc.● Works collaboratively as a department to ensure optimal performance and productivity. Manages and maintains existing gardens and grounds - to include laying mulch, planting, turning over garden beds, weeding, deadheading, tilling, transplanting or dividing perennials, watering, fertilizing, hauling brush, mowing, raking, applying soil amendments, and maintaining a variety of woody and herbaceous plants.● Helps create a visually pleasing and safe garden year-round.● Records planting activity to ensure updated and correct plant records.● Responsible for correctly training on and use of garden equipment. Maintains all garden equipment in exceptional condition to optimize performance/longevity. Reports immediately any broken/unusable equipment.● Practices and maintains environmentally friendly and sustainable garden practices in all areas. Research best practices when it is unknown, to include evaluating other gardens and organizations.● Conduct tours, present lectures or write on horticulture topics for outreach use when asked. Looks for opportunities to increase knowledge in horticulture. ● Maneuver in narrow or confined spaces. Must work outdoors in all weather conditions and routinely lift up to 40 pounds. Must be able to bend, squat, lift, push, and pull and move in a variety of positions. Able to walk over varied terrains.Other Functions● While main duties include horticulture activities, it is expected that team members work collaboratively to ensure all garden events are adequately supported. This would include setup and tear down of both public and private events, some facility maintenance, and installation of major exhibits.● Interact with the public to give exceptional visitor experience.● Attend staff meetings and other staff initiatives.● Other duties as assigned.Job Requirements: Minimum QualificationsSkills, Knowledge and Abilities● Must be majoring in Horticulture or other related degree, and/or proven equivalent experience.● Public Garden experience preferred, desired and given preference to.● Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills, excellent interpersonal abilities, demonstrated time management skills, and the ability to deal effectively with the public, to include other staff & volunteers.● Computer literacy, to include MS Office applications.● Knowledge of GA cultivated and native plants and their cultivation requirements, or a willingness to learn quickly.● Operate a variety of small machinery and power equipment including utility vehicle, pruners, sheers, weed eaters, sprayers, blowers and push and riding mowers.● Makes decisions and uses sound judgment appropriate for level of responsibility.● Follows safety guidelines to ensure a safe working environment & consistently demonstrates safe work behaviors.Working EnvironmentThe usual and customary methods of performing the job's functions require the following physical demands: lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling; some climbing and balancing; some stooping, kneeling, crouching, and/or crawling; and significant fine finger dexterity in all outdoor weather conditions and in narrow or confined spaces. Generally, the job requires 10% sitting, 45% walking, and 45% standing. This job is performed generally outdoors where the ambient temperature spans 25-100 degrees Fahrenheit. HOW TO APPLY:To Apply: Please submit a cover letter or statement of interest, résumé, and three references. Submit by email tocomuhr@comuga.org. No phone calls or in person applications accepted.Required Testing Certificates & LicensesNone Specified 2-year Horticulture or other related degree, or proven equivalent experienceContinuing Educ. / Training ClearancesAs funding permits Criminal Justice Fingerprint/Background ClearanceSalary Grade$12-14 per hour for an intern position

jobs.description: Employer: Ryan Companies Expires: 09/06/2026 Ryan Companies has an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Field Engineer Intern. jobs.title: Horticulture Intern at The Columbus Museum
jobs.description: Employer: The Columbus Museum Expires: 09/06/2026 Purpose StatementThe Columbus Museum is a mature, successful art and history museum with an Olmsted historic garden in a growing community in West Central Georgia with many cultural amenities.The ideal candidate will work as a team member, performing a variety of skilled and semi-skilled landscape tasks to implement the maintenance and planting of natural areas, grounds and garden beds according to plans. This position is non-exempt and will include both weekday and weekend hours. Hours TBD upon hiring. Must work outdoors in all weather conditions and routinely lift up to 40 pounds. Essential Functions ● Adheres and promotes the mission, vision and values of The Columbus Museum, Inc.● Works collaboratively as a department to ensure optimal performance and productivity. Manages and maintains existing gardens and grounds - to include laying mulch, planting, turning over garden beds, weeding, deadheading, tilling, transplanting or dividing perennials, watering, fertilizing, hauling brush, mowing, raking, applying soil amendments, and maintaining a variety of woody and herbaceous plants.● Helps create a visually pleasing and safe garden year-round.● Records planting activity to ensure updated and correct plant records.● Responsible for correctly training on and use of garden equipment. Maintains all garden equipment in exceptional condition to optimize performance/longevity. Reports immediately any broken/unusable equipment.● Practices and maintains environmentally friendly and sustainable garden practices in all areas. Research best practices when it is unknown, to include evaluating other gardens and organizations.● Conduct tours, present lectures or write on horticulture topics for outreach use when asked. Looks for opportunities to increase knowledge in horticulture. ● Maneuver in narrow or confined spaces. Must work outdoors in all weather conditions and routinely lift up to 40 pounds. Must be able to bend, squat, lift, push, and pull and move in a variety of positions. Able to walk over varied terrains.Other Functions● While main duties include horticulture activities, it is expected that team members work collaboratively to ensure all garden events are adequately supported. This would include setup and tear down of both public and private events, some facility maintenance, and installation of major exhibits.● Interact with the public to give exceptional visitor experience.● Attend staff meetings and other staff initiatives.● Other duties as assigned.Job Requirements: Minimum QualificationsSkills, Knowledge and Abilities● Must be majoring in Horticulture or other related degree, and/or proven equivalent experience.● Public Garden experience preferred, desired and given preference to.● Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills, excellent interpersonal abilities, demonstrated time management skills, and the ability to deal effectively with the public, to include other staff & volunteers.● Computer literacy, to include MS Office applications.● Knowledge of GA cultivated and native plants and their cultivation requirements, or a willingness to learn quickly.● Operate a variety of small machinery and power equipment including utility vehicle, pruners, sheers, weed eaters, sprayers, blowers and push and riding mowers.● Makes decisions and uses sound judgment appropriate for level of responsibility.● Follows safety guidelines to ensure a safe working environment & consistently demonstrates safe work behaviors.Working EnvironmentThe usual and customary methods of performing the job's functions require the following physical demands: lifting, carrying, pushing, and/or pulling; some climbing and balancing; some stooping, kneeling, crouching, and/or crawling; and significant fine finger dexterity in all outdoor weather conditions and in narrow or confined spaces. Generally, the job requires 10% sitting, 45% walking, and 45% standing. This job is performed generally outdoors where the ambient temperature spans 25-100 degrees Fahrenheit. HOW TO APPLY:To Apply: Please submit a cover letter or statement of interest, résumé, and three references. Submit by email tocomuhr@comuga.org. No phone calls or in person applications accepted.Required Testing Certificates & LicensesNone Specified 2-year Horticulture or other related degree, or proven equivalent experienceContinuing Educ. / Training ClearancesAs funding permits Criminal Justice Fingerprint/Background ClearanceSalary Grade$12-14 per hour for an intern position

If you’re the kind of student who likes figuring out how things work, why they work, and what to do when they don’t, this is a great place to spend your internship.WHAT WE OFFER.$22.00 per hour.Flexibility to work around your school schedule and ideally, put in 16 hours per week in-office.Remote work is not available.WHAT YOUR DAYS WILL LOOK LIKE.Depending on your background, interests, and assigned projects, you may:Learn and apply SGR’s engineering, scientific, and software-development procedures.Assist with preparing CAD geometry and generating or reviewing meshes for computational analysis.Configure, run, and monitor existing computational tools under the guidance of experienced team members.Develop, modify, and test scripts or software using Python, MATLAB, C/C++, or other programming languages appropriate to your background.Support laboratory, field-test, and measurement activities, including equipment preparation, data collection, data organization, and documentation.Compare computational results with measured data and help investigate why the two may not always agree.Work methodically through unfamiliar technical problems while learning how experienced engineers and scientists approach them.Ask questions, receive feedback, improve your work, and keep learning along the way.WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR.Must be currently enrolled in a scientific or technical college or university degree program such as Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or a related field.Someone curious, dependable, and willing to learn—especially when the problem in front of you doesn’t come with an obvious answer.You are comfortable receiving coaching, asking questions, and using feedback to improve your work.Willing to stick with challenging technical problems and work through them thoughtfully.Any experience with: CAD tools (such as SolidWorks or Rhino), animation software (Blender) , MATLAB, Python, C/C++, computational modeling and simulation, engineering analysis, laboratory work, or technical research is a plus.Class projects, research, internships, competition teams, and personal projects all count. We’re interested in what you’ve tried, what you’ve learned, and what you’re excited to learn next.A valid driver’s.U.S. citizenship is required, along with the ability to obtain a security clearance. Don’t have clearance? No problem—we’ll help you through the process.ARE YOU READY to put your curiosity to work? Apply today at signatureresearch.hirescore.com———————————-At SGR, we’re a small but innovative high-tech company with offices in Calumet, Michigan, and Navarre, Florida, specializing in multi-spectral data collection, analysis, modeling, and software development. As a small business, we value work-life balance and celebrate our team’s achievements with bonuses, events, and gatherings. If you’re looking for challenging, exciting work in a supportive and dynamic atmosphere, SGR is the place for you. SGR is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Layout Engineer Intern at Concrete Strategies
jobs.description: Employer: Concrete Strategies Expires: 09/12/2026 Layout Engineer Intern CONCRETE STRATEGIES - Nationwide, USA, United StatesTagged: InternshipAs a Layout Engineer Intern at Concrete Strategies, you'll be immersed in the critical aspect of translating design plans into real-world construction. Your role involves mastering the art of precise measurements, spatial alignment, and layout implementation to ensure the accurate placement of structures and components on the construction site.During your internship, you'll have the opportunity to learn about and contribute to:Blueprint Interpretation: Learn to interpret architectural and engineering blueprints, understanding the spatial relationships and dimensions depicted in the plans. jobs.title: LVDT/RVDT Engineering Intern at RAM Aerospace
jobs.description: Employer: RAM Aerospace Expires: 09/12/2026 RAM Aerospace is a leader in aerospace innovation, powering flight and space exploration with precision solenoids, valves, actuators, and position sensing solutions. Since 1975, we've supported missions like the Space Shuttle and continue to deliver mission-critical components for commercial, defense, and satellite systems. Headquartered in St. George, Utah, our advanced manufacturing facility produces the precision solenoids, valves, and actuators that aerospace programs worldwide depend on. Our Valencia facility extends that capability with specialized manufacturing of LVDTs and RVDTs, critical position sensing devices used across a broad range of aerospace and defense applications. As one of Southern Utah's largest employers, we drive economic growth and offer high-skilled careers in engineering and manufacturing. From both facilities, we build the future of aerospace—on time, with excellence, and as a team. Join us to work on groundbreaking technology and help shape the future of flight and space exploration. Your career takes off here!RAM Aerospace's LVDT/RVDT Intern program is built for engineering students who want more than a summer project. This is a year-round, part-time position designed to fit alongside your academic schedule, giving you sustained, meaningful exposure to the design, analysis, test, and manufacturing of Linear Variable Differential Transformers, the precision position sensing devices that aerospace and defense systems worldwide depend on. You will work directly alongside experienced engineers and technicians, contributing to real work on real hardware across multiple disciplines. By the time you finish school, you will have built a level of hands-on aerospace engineering experience that very few of your peers can match. If you are an engineering student who is eager to learn, ready to contribute, and looking for a role that grows with you through your academic career, this opportunity was built for you.Duties and ResponsibilitiesDesign & Engineering Support: Assist RAM engineers in the design and development of LVDT/RVDT components and assemblies. Support CAD modeling, drawing updates, and design documentation using 3D CAD tools, and contribute to design reviews and engineering analysis tasks as your skills and familiarity with the product grow over time.Analysis & Performance Modeling: Support engineering analysis efforts related to LVDT/RVDT performance, including electromagnetic behavior, dimensional tolerance reviews, and basic mechanical assessments. Learn to apply analytical tools and methods under the guidance of senior engineers, building a working understanding of how design decisions translate into measurable performance outcomes.Test Support & Data Collection: Assist in the setup, execution, and documentation of LVDT/RVDT performance and functional testing. Operate test equipment under supervision, collect and log test data accurately, and support the analysis and reporting of test results in a format that informs engineering decisions.Manufacturing & Assembly Support: Work alongside technicians in the assembly of LVDT/RVDT components and subassemblies, learning proper assembly techniques, workmanship standards, and the attention to detail that precision aerospace hardware demands. Support manufacturing operations in a manner that reinforces RAM's quality and FOD prevention standards at all times.Documentation & Continuous Learning: Maintain accurate records of engineering and assembly activities in accordance with RAM's quality management system requirements. Engage actively with the engineers and technicians around you, ask good questions, take ownership of your development, and bring growing capability and initiative to your work with each passing semester.RequirementsLegal: Must be able to pass a comprehensive criminal background check and drug screening.ITAR: Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum (due to ITAR requirements).Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's degree program in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related field required.Minimum sophomore standing required. Junior or senior standing preferred.Basic understanding of electromagnetic or electromechanical principles gained through coursework is a plus.Exposure to 3D CAD software through coursework or personal projects preferred. SolidWorks experience a plus.Ability to read and interpret basic engineering drawings and written assembly procedures.Strong attention to detail and genuine commitment to accuracy in both hands-on work and documentation.Ability to commit to a consistent part-time schedule throughout the academic year, with flexibility to increase hours during breaks if desired.Eager to learn, self-motivated, and comfortable working in an active manufacturing and engineering environment alongside experienced professionals.Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document work accurately and collaborate effectively with engineers and technicians.We are committed to creating an environment where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally.EEO (Equal Employment Opportunity)RAM Aerospace is an equal opportunity employer. All aspects of employment including the decision to hire, promote, discipline, or discharge, will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law. In addition, it is the policy of RAM Aerospace to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.We welcome former military and law enforcement applicants!

jobs.title: Field Engineer Intern at Ballard Marine Construction
jobs.description: Employer: Ballard Marine Construction Expires: 09/12/2026 WHY JOIN BALLARD MARINE CONSTRUCTION? At Ballard, we believe the best way to learn is by doing. That's why we empower our team members at every level to take ownership, contribute ideas, and make an impact. As a specialty marine and heavy civil contractor, we take on some of the industry's most unique and challenging projects across North America. Our success is built on a culture of accountability, teamwork, grit, and continuous improvement. We challenge each other to be our best, celebrate our successes together, and never stop looking for ways to improve. If you're looking for an organization that values hard work, invests in its people, and provides opportunities to grow alongside some of the best professionals in the industry, Ballard may be the right place for you. Job Summary: The Field Engineer Intern supports marine and heavy civil construction projects through a combination of field and office-based experiences. Working alongside experienced engineers, project managers, and construction professionals, this role provides hands-on exposure to project planning, estimating, and scheduling while gaining meaningful experience on complex, high-impact projects. Interns will be immersed in Ballard’s collaborative, safety-first culture and have the opportunity to learn from industry leaders, build relationships, and develop the skills needed to launch a successful career in construction. This internship is designed to provide hands-on, real-world experience that accelerates your development as an engineer in the construction industry. Interns are immersed in Ballard's collaborative, safety-first culture and have the opportunity to build technical expertise, strengthen problem-solving abilities, develop leadership skills, and contribute to work that directly impacts successful project delivery. Through mentorship, field exposure, and cross-functional collaboration, interns gain valuable industry experience and a strong foundation for a career in construction. We take on challenges that nobody else can; or will.Comradery and Inspirational - We are a hard-working team of likeminded individuals working toward a common goal. We regularly celebrate wins and like to have fun whether at work or at play. We come together each day looking for ways to instill life and energy into the world around us.Driven and Competitive - We love competition. We love to win and love to learn when we lose. Not getting the job done is not an option. We are obsessed to do our best and we do what it takes to win.Trustworthy and Respectful - We are passionate about honesty, authenticity, and transparency. No lies. No drama. No politics. We ask, “what could I have done differently?” and then we share lessons learned. Regularly challenging ourselves and those around us to be better is a way of life. “Me first” belongs here. Education: Currently enrolled in an accredited bachelor's degree program in Construction Management, Construction Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a related field.Must have completed at least two years of coursework (sophomore standing or higher) by the start of the internship. jobs.title: Growth Intern at Photon
jobs.description: Employer: Photon Expires: 09/12/2026 About PhotonPhoton is the infrastructure behind production-ready messaging agents — connecting AI, conversations, and real-world actions across iMessage, WhatsApp, Telegram, and more.Thousands of developers build on Photon today. So do startups like Ditto, FlipText, and Folk, and scale-ups like Rho, Minimax, and Nous Research (Hermes).We're also the team behind some of the most talked-about events in San Francisco — the Photon Residency and GoKarting through SF among them — which have reached millions of viewers and turned a developer tool into something people actually want to be part of.The rolePhoton is growing 2–3x month-over-month, and the ceiling on this role is set entirely by what you decide to go do. You'll sit close to the founders, close to the engineers, and close to the customers. If you have an idea on Monday, the expectation is that some version of it is live by Friday.What you'll doWork directly with the companies defining this space. You'll be in the room with the teams building on Photon — from three-person startups shipping their first agent to scale-ups running production traffic. You'll learn what they're building, help them ship it, and turn their wins into stories the rest of the market hears.Use the Photon brand as a stage. Photon Residency and GoKarting weren't marketing campaigns; they were ideas someone took seriously enough to execute. We want you bringing the next one. Hackathons, residencies, launches, things that don't have a name yet.Own a piece of the growth curve. 2–3x MoM doesn't sustain itself. You'll find the channels, run the experiments, kill what doesn't work, and pour fuel on what does. You'll be measured on outcomes, not activity.Open new verticals. Messaging agents are showing up in places nobody has mapped yet. You'll pick a wedge, build the thesis, run the first motions, and tell us whether it's real.You might be a fit ifYou've shipped something on your own. Scale matters less than the fact that you started it.You write well and quickly. Most of growth here is producing ideas.You can commute to SF.You'd rather be given a problem than a task list.

jobs.description: Employer: Custom Courts Construction Expires: 09/13/2026 SketchUp Designer – Sports Court Design & RenderingsCustom Courts Construction is seeking a skilled SketchUp Designer to create professional drawings, layouts, and 3D renderings for tennis courts, pickleball courts, basketball courts, and other athletic facilities.This position will work closely with our estimating and project management team to turn site measurements, customer concepts, plans, and project information into clear and professional visual presentations.ResponsibilitiesCreate detailed 2D and 3D sports court layouts using SketchUp.Produce professional 3D renderings for customer presentations and proposals.Develop accurate court layouts using provided site dimensions and measurements.Lay out tennis, pickleball, basketball, and multi-sport playing areas to specified dimensions.Show court orientation, playing lines, run-off areas, and surrounding improvements.Incorporate fencing, gates, net posts, basketball goals, lighting, retaining walls, walkways, drainage features, and other site elements.Create different court color and layout options for customers.Produce overhead/site-plan views as well as perspective renderings.Add dimensions, labels, notes, and other information necessary to clearly communicate the proposed design.Revise drawings and renderings based on customer or project-team feedback.Maintain organized SketchUp files and reusable models/components for commonly used court equipment and construction details.Export presentation-quality PDFs and image files for proposals, contracts, customer approvals, and marketing.Work from architectural drawings, surveys, aerial imagery, photographs, hand sketches, and field measurements provided by our team.Typical ProjectsDesign work may include:Residential tennis and pickleball courtsCommercial and HOA athletic facilitiesMulti-court tennis and pickleball complexesBasketball courtsMulti-sport courtsPost-tension concrete court layoutsFencing and gate configurationsSports lighting layoutsCourt equipment locationsDrainage and surrounding site improvementsCourt resurfacing and color-layout conceptsQualificationsStrong proficiency in SketchUp.Experience producing professional 3D models and renderings.Ability to create accurate drawings from dimensions and field measurements.Strong understanding of scale, dimensions, proportions, and site layouts.Ability to turn rough sketches and concepts into polished customer-facing drawings.Detail-oriented and able to identify dimensional or layout conflicts.Comfortable making revisions quickly as project designs evolve.Experience with architectural, landscape, construction, or sports-facility design is preferred.Experience with rendering software such as Enscape, V-Ray, Lumion, or similar is a plus.AutoCAD experience is a plus but not required.What We're Looking ForWe are looking for someone who can do more than simply build a SketchUp model. The goal is to create accurate, professional drawings and realistic renderings that help customers visualize exactly what their finished court will look like before construction begins.The right person should be able to take basic project information—such as a survey, measurements, photos, and a description of the proposed court—and turn it into a polished layout and presentation that our sales and construction teams can use with customers.

jobs.title: Services - Summer Analyst Program, New York City - US, 2027 at Citi
jobs.description: Employer: Citi Expires: 09/13/2026 You're the brains behind our work.You’re ready to bring your knowledge from the classroom to the workplace, and Citi wants to help you get there. Whether it’s honing your skills or building your network, we know that success comes with growth. Our program equips you with the knowledge and training you need to play a valuable role on your team and establish a long-term career here. At Citi, we value internal mobility—career growth is not a question of if, but when. What is Services?Citi’s Services organization plays a crucial role in supporting institutional clients through a wide range of innovative solutions, enabling them to navigate complex financial landscapes. Our business provides integrated cash management and trade finance solutions to help multinational corporations, financial institutions, and public sector organizations optimize liquidity, working capital, and streamline transactions globally. Our business also delivers custody, fund administration, collateral management, and performance analytics, helping asset managers, institutional investors, and financial institutions efficiently manage and safeguard assets. With our global reach, including presence in over 90 countries, cutting-edge technology, and client-first approach, we provide seamless solutions that drive business success in an evolving financial world.In this rapidly evolving landscape, we are increasingly leveraging advanced analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance our offerings, improve efficiency, and provide deeper insights to our clients. This includes utilizing AI-powered tools for predictive analytics, automation of routine tasks, and generating actionable insights from vast datasets to inform strategic decisions across our services portfolio. We provide you with the knowledge and skills you need to succeed.The Citi Services 10-week Summer Analyst Program gives entry-level employees hands-on experience through training sessions and real, on-the-job learning. Summer Analysts work closely with their teams, owning projects that drive meaningful impact. After an initial week of training and a placement process based on your interests and our needs, you’ll be assigned to a team where you’ll focus on financial analysis, business development, client engagement, and market research. Your time here will look something like this:Conduct market research to assess industry trends and the impact of macroeconomic factors.Develop materials that support business development, product commercialization, and revenue growth, identifying opportunities where data-driven insights and AI capabilities can add value. This may involve contributing to business cases for new AI-driven product features or improvements to existing services.Assist with process optimization initiatives to enhance efficiency and mitigate risk, potentially exploring how AI/ML tools can automate tasks or improve decision-making. Evaluate the effectiveness of AI-powered automation in improving operational workflows and reducing manual effort.Analyze client data to identify opportunities and improve service offerings, leveraging various analytical techniques, including interpreting insights derived from advanced analytical models. You will be exposed to how AI models are used to segment clients, predict behaviors, and personalize service delivery.Prepare reports and presentations for internal stakeholders and senior leadership, effectively communicating complex data analysis and potentially insights from AI-driven tools. Clearly articulate the implications and benefits of AI-generated insights for business strategies.Participate in networking events, training sessions, and leadership discussions to strengthen your personal and professional development. We want to hear from you if…You are a junior in college, graduating between December 2027 and May 2028, with a preferred GPA of 3.5 or above.You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills.You are proficient in Microsoft Excel (e.g., data analysis, lookups, basic modeling) and have working knowledge of PowerPoint and Outlook. Exposure to analytical platforms or an eagerness to learn about AI-specific tools (e.g., natural language processing applications, machine learning dashboards) will be beneficial.You have an interest in financial services and a drive to learn how technology, including AI, is transforming the industry. Demonstrated curiosity about how AI is being leveraged for efficiency, client experience, and risk management is key. You do not require sponsorship for U.S. work authorization now or in the future. Who we think will be a great fit…We’re looking for motivated individuals who are eager to start their careers at a global organization, tend to think strategically, have an innovative approach to business, and value diversity as much as we do. We know that anyone—not just those with business degrees—can have a knack for business, so we’re open to all disciplines. We’ll also be looking for:Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.Excellent communication skills.A high level of accuracy, time management, and attention to detail, including a proactive interest in understanding AI methodologies and their application in real-world business scenarios.Solid organizational skills and ability to work autonomously – self-starter.A high level of personal integrity, commitment to excellence, and a strong desire to learn.Resilience to thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.A sense of urgency and the ability to execute quickly and efficiently. Your future at CitiSuccessful Summer Analysts may be invited to return as full-time Analysts upon graduation. During the program, you will have access to mentorship, career development sessions, and networking opportunities with senior leaders and professionals across Citi. This experience is designed to provide you with a strong foundation to launch a long-term career within the firm, preparing you for a future where technology and AI play an increasingly central role. You will develop skills that are not only relevant today but are also essential for navigating the evolving landscape of AI-driven financial services. Join us and take the first step toward shaping the future of Citi!

jobs.title: Code and Zoning Interpretation Intern at NYC Department of Buildings
jobs.description: Employer: NYC Department of Buildings Expires: 09/13/2026 Code and Zoning Interpretation Intern About usAt the NYC Department of Buildings, we are responsible for ensuring the safe and lawful use of buildings and properties by enforcing the NYC Construction Codes, Energy Code and Zoning Resolution. We facilitate compliant development with integrity, efficiency and professionalism. As an agency, we are committed to remaining a premier municipal building organization, dedicated to enhancing the quality of life for all New Yorkers and making our city safer. As an employer, we are committed to improving our performance and developing procedures that are streamlined, understandable, and transparent.About the teamThe Code & Zoning Interpretation unit is responsible for the interpretation of the NYC Construction Codes, NYC Electrical Code, NYC Zoning Resolution, NYS Multiple Dwelling Law, and related laws and rules. The unit responds to interpretation requests, trains examiners on code and zoning, and manages appeals of determinations made by the borough offices.The Code and Zoning Interpretation intern will:- Assist with coordinating code development meetings and following up in a timely manner on matters requiring further action.- Assist with the creation of technical material for code committee review- Tracking code committee progress.- Assist with coordinating training sessions for industry stakeholders, DOB and other city-wide staff regarding code.- Assist with creation and maintenance of databases, spreadsheets and tracking systems, tables, charts, graphs, and presentations related to code development.- Drafting meeting summaries and status reports for tracking purposes; preparing documents for local law formatting.- Performing research regarding national standards and codes of other jurisdictions.- Scheduling and attending meetings, including inter-agency, division, and industry.Work Hours17 hours/week when school is in session35 hours/week when school is on breakPAY RATESEntering Freshmen through completion of Sophomore year: $17.50Entering Junior through completion of Senior year: $17.75Graduate level: $18.00REMOTE WORKWhen working a 35 hour/week schedule, this position may be eligible for remote work up to 2 days per week, pursuant to the Remote Work Pilot ProgramCOLLEGE AIDE (ALL CITY DEPTS) - 10209 Minimum Qualifications For Assignment Level I:Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school.For Assignment Level II (Information Technology):Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or closely related field, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study.For Assignment Level III (Information Technology Fellow):Matriculation at an accredited college or graduate school. Employment is conditioned upon continuance as a student in a college or graduate school with a specific course of study in information technology, computer science, management information systems, data processing, or other area relevant to the information technology project(s) assigned, including or supplemented by 9 semester credits in an acceptable course of study. Appointments to this Assignment Level will be made by the Technology Steering Committee through the Department of Information Technology and Telecommunications.SPECIAL NOTEMaximum tenure for all Assignment Levels in the title of College Aide is 6 years. No student shall be employed more than half-time in any week in which classes in which the student is enrolled are in session. Students may be employed full-time during their vacation periods. Preferred SkillsShould be majoring in Architecture, Engineering, City Planning, Urban Studies, or a related field Excellent written and verbal communication skills Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint Public Service Loan ForgivenessAs a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal loan forgiveness programs and state repayment assistance programs. For more information, please visit the U.S. Department of Education’s website at https://studentaid.gov/pslf/. Residency RequirementNew York City residency is generally required within 90 days of appointment. However, City Employees in certain titles who have worked for the City for 2 continuous years may also be eligible to reside in Nassau, Suffolk, Putnam, Westchester, Rockland, or Orange County. To determine if the residency requirement applies to you, please discuss with the agency representative at the time of interview. Additional Information The City of New York is an inclusive equal opportunity employer committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse workforce and providing a work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment based upon any legally protected status or protected characteristic, including but not limited to an individual's sex, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, gender identity, or pregnancy.
